cases.translation: He was a pedant of the highest degree.
cases.explain: Педант is the predicate noun after Это был ("He was"), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: До сих пор любуюсь, вспоминая истинно джентльменский, добродушный, открытый тон моего ___.
cases.translation: To this day I admire, recalling the truly gentlemanly, good-natured, open tone of my letter.
cases.explain: Письма depends on the noun тон ("the tone OF the letter"), a possessive relationship expressed by the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Толкался я больше по самым людным промышленным ___.
cases.translation: I mostly wandered along the busiest, most industrial streets.
cases.explain: The preposition по ("along") governs the dative case, hence улицам (plural of улица).

cases.sentence: Развязно и самодовольно, придя домой, я немедленно написал ___.
cases.translation: Casually and self-satisfied, having come home, I immediately wrote out the note.
cases.explain: Сигнал is the direct object of the transitive verb написал ("wrote"), so it takes the accusative case (identical in form to the nominative for this inanimate noun).

cases.sentence: Что-то не умирало во мне внутри ... и сказывалось жгучей ___.
cases.translation: Something inside me refused to die ... and expressed itself as a burning anguish.
cases.explain: The verb сказывалось ("made itself known/manifested") governs the instrumental case of manner, hence тоской.

cases.sentence: Что-то не умирало во мне внутри, в ___ сердца и совести.
cases.translation: Something inside me refused to die, in the depths of my heart and conscience.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the prepositional case, hence глубине.

reading.ru: Я, впрочем, не скоро согласился признать эту истину.
reading.question: How quickly did the narrator accept this uncomfortable truth?
options: Not quickly — it took him a while
reading.correct: Not quickly — it took him a while
reading.explain: The text says я, впрочем, не скоро согласился признать эту истину — he was not quick to admit this truth.

reading.ru: Ведь нападет же такое бабье расстройство.
reading.question: How does the narrator dismiss his own emotional outburst from the night before?
options: As a silly, womanish fit of distress that came over him
As a sign of true love
reading.correct: As a silly, womanish fit of distress that came over him
reading.explain: He scoffs Ведь нападет же такое бабье расстройство — such a womanish upset can just come over one.

reading.ru: Надо было спешить и во что бы то ни стало, скорее спасать мою репутацию в глазах Зверкова и Симонова.
reading.question: What did the narrator feel was urgently necessary the next morning?
options: To save his reputation in the eyes of Zverkov and Simonov
To move to a new apartment
reading.correct: To save his reputation in the eyes of Zverkov and Simonov
reading.explain: He feels he must скорее спасать мою репутацию в глазах Зверкова и Симонова — quickly save his reputation with Zverkov and Simonov.

reading.ru: Я решился на отчаянное средство, занять целых 15 рублей у Антона Антоновича.
reading.question: What desperate measure does the narrator take to pay off his debt?
options: Borrowing fifteen rubles from Anton Antonovich
reading.correct: Borrowing fifteen rubles from Anton Antonovich
reading.explain: He decides on Я решился на отчаянное средство, занять целых 15 рублей у Антона Антоновича — borrowing fifteen rubles from Anton Antonovich.

reading.ru: Развязно и самодовольно, придя домой, я немедленно написал сигнал.
reading.question: What did the narrator do as soon as he got home, feeling pleased with himself?
options: He immediately wrote out a note/letter
reading.correct: He immediately wrote out a note/letter
reading.explain: The text says придя домой, я немедленно написал сигнал — coming home, he immediately wrote out the note (to Simonov).

reading.ru: «Я обвинил себя во всем», — оправдывался я.
reading.question: How does the narrator excuse himself in his letter to Simonov?
options: By saying he blamed himself for everything
reading.correct: By saying he blamed himself for everything
reading.explain: He writes «Я обвинил себя во всем» — "I blamed myself for everything" — to excuse his behavior.

reading.ru: Я вложил в письмо шесть рублей, запечатал и упросил Аполлона снести к Симонову.
reading.question: What did the narrator put inside the letter before sending it?
reading.correct: Six rubles
reading.explain: The text says Я вложил в письмо шесть рублей — he put six rubles inside the letter.

reading.ru: Узнав, что в письме деньги, Аполлон стал почтительнее и согласился сходить.
reading.question: How did Apollon's attitude change once he learned there was money in the letter?
options: He became more respectful and agreed to deliver it
reading.correct: He became more respectful and agreed to deliver it
reading.explain: The text says Узнав, что в письме деньги, Аполлон стал почтительнее и согласился сходить — learning there was money inside, Apollon became more respectful and agreed to go.

reading.ru: К вечеру я вышел пройтись.
reading.question: What did the narrator do as evening approached?
options: He went out for a walk
reading.correct: He went out for a walk
reading.explain: The text says К вечеру я вышел пройтись — toward evening he went out for a walk.

reading.ru: Толкался я больше по самым людным промышленным улицам, по Мещанским, по Садовой, у Юсупова сада.
reading.question: Where did the narrator wander most during his walk?
options: The busiest, most industrial streets, like Meshchanskaya and Sadovaya
reading.correct: The busiest, most industrial streets, like Meshchanskaya and Sadovaya
reading.explain: He says he wandered по самым людным промышленным улицам, по Мещанским, по Садовой — along the busiest, most industrial streets.

reading.ru: Мучила меня постоянно мысль, что придет Лиза.
reading.question: What thought constantly tormented the narrator that evening?
options: That Simonov would refuse his apology
That he would lose his job
reading.correct: That Liza would come
reading.explain: He says Мучила меня постоянно мысль, что придет Лиза — the thought that Liza would come constantly tormented him.

reading.ru: Просто нищета в квартире.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the state of his apartment, worrying about Liza seeing it?
reading.correct: Simply poverty/destitution in the apartment
reading.explain: He admits Просто нищета в квартире — it is simply poverty in the apartment, worrying what Liza will think.

reading.ru: Это когда я осветил спичкой комнату и увидал ее бледное, искривленное лицо с мученическим взглядом.
reading.question: Which particular memory of the previous night especially haunted the narrator?
options: Lighting the room with a match and seeing her pale, twisted, martyred face
reading.correct: Lighting the room with a match and seeing her pale, twisted, martyred face
reading.explain: He recalls the moment когда я осветил спичкой комнату и увидал ее бледное, искривленное лицо с мученическим взглядом — lighting the room and seeing her pale, twisted, suffering face.

reading.ru: На другой день я уже опять готов был считать все это вздором, развозившимися нервами, а главное преувеличением.
reading.question: How did the narrator's view of the previous night's events change the next day?
options: He was ready to dismiss it all as nonsense, frayed nerves, and exaggeration
He decided it was the most important night of his life
He resolved to marry Liza immediately
He decided to move away from the city
reading.correct: He was ready to dismiss it all as nonsense, frayed nerves, and exaggeration
reading.explain: He says he was again ready считать все это вздором, развозившимися нервами, а главное преувеличением — to consider it all nonsense, frayed nerves, and mainly exaggeration.

reading.ru: «Придет, непременно придет!» — восклицал я, бегая по комнате.
reading.question: What did the narrator exclaim while pacing his room, anxious about Liza?
options: "She will come, she will certainly come!"
reading.correct: "She will come, she will certainly come!"
reading.explain: He exclaims «Придет, непременно придет!» while pacing the room — "She will come, she will certainly come!"

reading.ru: Прошел однако же день, другой, третий, она не приходила.
reading.question: What happened over the following days regarding Liza's visit?
options: A day, then another, then a third passed, and she did not come
She arrived the very next morning
She sent a letter instead of visiting
He went to visit her himself
reading.correct: A day, then another, then a third passed, and she did not come
reading.explain: The text says Прошел однако же день, другой, третий, она не приходила — a day passed, then another, then a third, and she did not come.

reading.ru: Я, например, спасаю Лизу именно тем, что она ко мне ходит.
reading.question: What fantasy does the narrator entertain about "saving" Liza?
options: That he saves her precisely by having her visit him and be educated by him
That he saves her by giving her money
That he saves her by marrying her secretly
That he saves her by reporting the brothel to police
reading.correct: That he saves her precisely by having her visit him and be educated by him
reading.explain: He imagines Я, например, спасаю Лизу именно тем, что она ко мне ходит — he saves Liza precisely by her coming to visit him, so he can educate her.

reading.ru: Человек он был пожилой, важный, занимавшийся отчасти... партняжеством, но неизвестно почему он презирал меня даже сверх всякой меры и смотрел на меня нестерпимо свысока.
reading.question: How is Apollon, the servant, first described?
options: An elderly, self-important man who dabbled partly in tailoring
reading.correct: An elderly, self-important man who dabbled partly in tailoring
reading.explain: The text describes Apollon as Человек он был пожилой, важный, занимавшийся отчасти... партняжеством — an elderly, self-important man, partly occupied with tailoring.

reading.ru: Это был педант в высочайшей степени.
reading.question: What quality does the narrator ascribe to Apollon above all others he has met?
options: He was a pedant to the highest degree
He was the kindest man alive
reading.correct: He was a pedant to the highest degree
reading.explain: The narrator says Это был педант в высочайшей степени — he was a pedant of the highest degree.

reading.ru: Он был влюблен в каждую пуговицу свою, в каждую свою ноготь.
reading.question: What does the narrator say Apollon was "in love" with?
options: Every one of his own buttons and every one of his own nails
reading.correct: Every one of his own buttons and every one of his own nails
reading.explain: The text says Он был влюблен в каждую пуговицу свою, в каждую свою ноготь — he was in love with every button and every nail of his own.

reading.ru: У него был язык несколько длиннее, чем следует, или что-то вроде этого.
reading.question: What physical peculiarity of Apollon's tongue does the narrator mention, explaining his lisp?
options: His tongue was somewhat longer than it should be
reading.correct: His tongue was somewhat longer than it should be
reading.explain: The narrator says У него был язык несколько длиннее, чем следует — his tongue was somewhat longer than it should be, causing his lisp.

reading.ru: Особенно бесил он меня, когда бывал начнет читать у себя за перегородкой псалтырь.
reading.question: What activity of Apollon's especially infuriated the narrator?
options: Reading the psalter aloud behind the partition
Talking to himself in the hallway
reading.correct: Reading the psalter aloud behind the partition
reading.explain: The narrator says Особенно бесил он меня, когда бывал начнет читать у себя за перегородкой псалтырь — Apollon especially enraged him when reading the psalter behind the partition.

reading.ru: Я положил не говорить ему об этом и даже нарочно молчать, чтобы победить его гордость и заставить его самого первого заговорить о жаловании.
reading.question: What plan does the narrator devise regarding Apollon's unpaid wages?
options: To stay silent deliberately to break Apollon's pride and force him to bring up wages first
To fire him on the spot
reading.correct: To stay silent deliberately to break Apollon's pride and force him to bring up wages first
reading.explain: He decides Я положил не говорить ему об этом ... чтобы победить его гордость и заставить его самого первого заговорить о жаловании — to stay silent to break Apollon's pride and make him speak of wages first.

reading.ru: «Стой!» — закричал я в выступлении, когда он медленно и молча повертывался с одной рукой за спиной, чтобы уйти в свою комнату.
reading.question: What did the narrator shout as Apollon began turning away silently?
reading.correct: "Stop!"
reading.explain: The narrator shouts «Стой!» as Apollon turns to leave silently with one hand behind his back.

reading.ru: В эту минуту мои часы принадлежались, прошипели и пробили семь.
reading.question: What happened with the clock at the very moment Liza appeared at the door?
options: It wheezed, hissed, and struck seven
reading.correct: It wheezed, hissed, and struck seven
reading.explain: The chapter ends with В эту минуту мои часы ... прошипели и пробили семь — at that moment the clock hissed and struck seven.
